name: passport-pantry
description: Travel-memory recipe app: country-first dish catalogue, canonical ingredient registry, allergen and diet engines, purchase-anchored pantry, and location-relative ingredient sourcing.

scripts.check: npm run test && npm run test:boundary && npm run test:ingest
scripts.start: echo "No server. Open prototype.html in a browser, or: npx http-server . -p 8000"

//: MODULE BOUNDARY — see docs/MODULE_BOUNDARY.md before changing this file.
dependencies and devDependencies are empty ON PURPOSE. The application is a
single self-contained HTML file and the tools are plain Node ES modules that
use only the standard library. Nothing here needs `npm install`; every script
above runs on a bare Node 18+. Adding the first dependency is a real decision,
not a convenience — it introduces a lockfile, an install step and a supply
chain to this module, and it is the point at which the separate-release-cycle
criterion in MODULE_BOUNDARY.md starts to apply.
This package is deliberately NOT registered in the root package.json's
`workspaces` field. The repository root is a fork of an unrelated upstream
project (jwangkun/Prompt-Tools); editing its manifest creates rebase conflicts
for no benefit, since a zero-dependency package gains nothing from hoisting.
Run these scripts from this directory. If one-command-from-root is ever wanted,
add workspaces then — it is reversible, and this comment is the argument
